transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what brought you in to see me?

I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up when I’m supposed to stay seated. Like during sprint planning at work, or even mortgage calls, I’ll know I should just sit and focus, but then I suddenly need water or decide I should check something in the other room. It’s been happening enough that it’s starting to feel like a problem.

When you feel that urge to get up and move, is it usually because you're feeling worried or on edge about something, or does it happen even when you're not particularly anxious—just a restless urge to move?

It happens even when I’m not especially anxious. I can look calm, but inside it feels like this pressure to move or switch tasks or do something with my hands. If I don’t, I start feeling really uncomfortable, like I’m going to crawl out of my skin.

Aside from the restlessness, do you also notice that your mind tends to wander or you get easily distracted when trying to focus on tasks, like losing track of what you were doing during those meetings?

Yes, that happens. I’ll start reviewing a pull request or reading through mortgage paperwork with good intentions, and then a few minutes later I realize I’m just staring at the same paragraph. My mind has gone off in like five unrelated directions, and I have to pull myself back and figure out where I even was.

Do you notice a pattern of getting into conflicts, breaking rules, or acting impulsively in ways that get you in trouble—at work, at home, or with others—beyond just the restlessness and distractibility you've described?

Not really, no. I don’t think of it as getting into trouble or breaking rules. I can be impatient or interrupt sometimes, but I’m not having conflicts with people in any major way. It’s more the restlessness and losing focus that’s been getting in my way.
Thinking back, did you notice similar restlessness or trouble focusing when you were a child, say before age 12, or is this something that's only become noticeable as an adult?

It was definitely there when I was a kid. I remember in elementary school teachers moving my desk or reminding me to stay seated because I was always popping up. I’d also talk before being called on or rush through work, even when I understood it. So, no, it’s not just an adult thing.
